The core mechanism operates through a two-phase process: (1) offline generation of a non-user-specific data structure mapping item similarities based on collective purchase behavior, and (2) online use of this structure to generate personalized recommendations. The first phase employs correlation analysis over purchase histories to compute similarity scores S_ij between items i and j. These scores are stored in a structured form such that step (c) retrieves sets of similar items for each known-interest item. Step (d) combines these sets, potentially applying weights based on user affinity (step 11) or filtering out prior purchases (step 11) or categories (step 12). The system avoids explicit user ratings (step 10), relying instead on implicit feedback. Temporal alignment ensures relevance (step 5), while cart-specific selection allows contextual recommendations (step 8). This dualism enables scalable, adaptive, and context-aware recommendation generation.
